title: PCB-D APRS

finish._cont_route_why: 11 September 2026: one continuation pass of the router before the stub router when a handful of connections are open (A21's lever of 5 September). cont_route.sh keeps the board only if it improves, so it cannot make one worse; it was declared for A alone because only the A clones carried it, and E and P both ended a route at exactly one open.
finish._cont_route_planes_why: 12 September 2026: the continuation exports its own DSN, and it did so with every plane REMOVED, because finish.sh passed it no plane treatment and routeflow never put one in the finish's environment either. That makes the continuation re-route every plane pin as a wire: on C that is GND on In1, the majority of the board's connections. It is the same treatment the route itself is given in routeflow/<phase>.json, and a test holds the two in agreement.
finish._return_via_why: 15 September 2026, owner ruling 20:15 CEST (appendix 32.198): a ground via within 1.5 mm of every signal via, fine-pitch escape fans exempt; the finish places them after the last copper-changing stage and the board gate (intent_checks item 4) refuses a board with a signal via left without one.
finish._via_parallel_why: 18 September 2026 (rule PI-003): after every copper-editing stage and before the ground vias, via_parallel lays parallel barrels beside any via dc_drop's solved mesh puts over IPC-2221's rating for its wall (the fabricator's 18 um plating), joined on every layer the net touches there, DRC-guarded, then re-solves and re-judges. On the committed board: D12 fails +5V_SA at 1.10 A against 0.90
finish._direct_close_why: BOARD D DECLARES THE DIRECT CLOSER FROM D15 (18 September 2026). Board D never needed it: D12 routed 0 hard and 0 unrouted. D15, which is D12's routability plus the locked copper that answers PI-003 at the two +5V_SA transitions, lands ONE connection open and both closers already in its finish refuse it: the continuation pass of the router reads 'before hard 0 unrouted 1, after hard 0 unrouted 1' over 80 passes, and the stub router says '/PCM_VDD pad -> track FAILED'. The gap is R28 pad 2 at (110.68, 105.80) to a 2.75 mm PCM_VDD track at (120.58, 109.90), **10.72 mm**, which is a connection the router never made rather than a closure it nearly made, so the third lever is the one board A and board E carry: a straight locked run the DRC decides on, tried on this board's two routing layers (In1 and In2 are planes here, so F.Cu and B.Cu are all there is) at a 12.0 mm reach with a 30 minute budget. It runs only where a board is open, it is DRC-guarded, and `guarded` puts the board back if it makes anything worse. NOTE: the D15 rounds in flight carry the tools their tree was staged with, so this reaches board D at a re-finish or at D16.

_phase_why: 12 September 2026: the phase is a fact about the board and it lived as a DEFAULT inside each generator, where gen_pcb_c.py still said C9 while the deliverable is C10, and full.sh set it for one board of six. A board's silk then names a phase `verify_deliverable` refuses, after the route, which is how A24 came to carry A18 on its front silk. `full.sh` exports this unless the caller has already set PHASE.
region_overflow_allow_mm_reason: D10 reads 0 hard on the placed board with PWR 0.0 mm and CTRL 0.2 mm outside their rectangles, measured 12 September 2026. Same rule: the number is what was measured, and zero is the target.
_gnd_grid_why: 15 September 2026 23:29 CEST, measured on D in /root/dgrid (decision 27, appendix 32.200): with 1,288 ground vias laid before the route the In2-plane D closed to 0 open after the stub router and the return-via gate read 279 of 289 signal vias with a ground via, against 138 of 185 when the fixer ran after the route with no room left. The grid is rule 2 by construction; it does nothing for rule 1.
_cont_route_planes_why: 15 September 2026: In2 is a ground plane on D (decision 27's measurement: two routing layers close the board, 0 hard 0 unrouted at every round), so the continuation route carries it as a power layer like the route.
_signal_classes_why: Rule RET-001, 16 September 2026. The return-path rule asks what a net's spectral content deserves, so every signal net needs a class and a reason. A net matched by no entry here is UNKNOWN and is judged at the STRICTEST bar, so an omission costs a failure rather than buying a pass. Patterns are shell globs over the net name without its leading slash, first match wins.

_annular_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, annular ring rows, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): four layers at 1 oz outer: multilayer 1 oz, recommended 0.20 mm or above. The RECOMMENDED figure is taken and not the absolute minimum, because the absolute minimum is where yield starts to suffer and this board is made five at a time with no second chance before the owner has it in his hands.
_via_ring_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002, the VIA rows rather than the annular ring row. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): minimum via diameter 0.25 mm on a minimum via hole of 0.15 mm for 2 or more layers, which leaves 0.05 mm of copper per side. The PTH annular ring row (0.20 mm) is stated for a plated COMPONENT hole and cannot bind a via, because no via at this document's own minimum could satisfy it; board D12 was refused on 16 September for a 0.45/0.20 via at 0.125 mm of ring, which is what that confusion costs.
_copper_layers_why: Four layers as built; decision 27 measured D with In2 as a plane rather than a routing layer, which is a fill decision inside the same stack and not a layer-count change.

external_ports.off_board: the PolyPhaser GTH-SFF-AL SMA surge arrestor at the antenna bulkhead (v2/vendor/polyphaser)
external_ports.why: the VHF antenna SMA: an outdoor conductor with a 30 W transmitter behind it, arrested in the wall rather than on the board
the power amplifier output to the antenna path, which reaches the same arrested bulkhead
a headset jack on the face, which a person plugs a headset into

_external_ports_why: Rule TRN-001, 16 September 2026. A port that leaves the ENCLOSURE is a wire a person will plug something into, in the rain, having walked across a floor. Every one of them reaches a semiconductor, and the only thing between is a suppressor, a choke, a series resistor into a clamp, or nothing. Most connectors on these boards are internal (board-to-board ribbons, module sockets, fan leads inside a sealed case) and treating every J as external would refuse every board for wires that never leave it. The board knows which is which and nothing else does, so each one is named with where it goes.

GND.what: the board's single ground: every return on this board is this net

_grounds_why: 16 September 2026, rule GND-001: either the board has one ground and says so, or every partition is drawn deliberately with its crossing points named and the signals that cross listed. ground_system.py reads the netlist and compares it with this.
critical_k_why: l = t_r / (6 t_pd). ECSS-E-HB-20-07A section 6.1.2.3 works a real case where a 35 mm clock track with a 200 ps edge failed a radiated emission test: that track is ONE rise distance long (t_r / t_pd = 34.5 mm on its microstrip), which is k = 1, and the handbook calls it a textbook radiator. k = 2 is half a known failure and k = 6 is a sixth of it. The number is this project's choice; the handbook is what it was calibrated against, and no standard in this tree states a value for k
_crystals_why: 16 September 2026, decision 37: this board's two 6 MHz crystals are not a part yet. The land it draws them on cannot hold a 6 MHz crystal (JLCPCB lists none in 3225 and a 6 MHz fundamental blank does not fit that case), and the code they were certified against is a 25 MHz part. Until the decision is ruled there is no C_L to declare, and an undeclared crystal reads INCONCLUSIVE, which is what this is.

Y1.source: TI SLLS413 (TUSB2046B) clause 8.3.2 and figure 6: the reference circuit is a 6 MHz fundamental crystal with a LOAD CAPACITANCE OF 20 pF, shunt capacitance at most 7 pF and ESR at most 50 Ohm, and TI chooses C1 = C2 = 27 pF for it 'in order to insure enough negative resistance', with Rd = 1.5 kOhm to trim the gain. So the 16.5 pF this board presents is the part maker's own under-load and not a miss: the same page is the source of both numbers. The PART is owner decision 37, because no passive 6 MHz crystal exists in the 3225 land this board draws, and whichever is bought must carry this C_L and an ESR its Rd is re-chosen for.

Y2.source: NOT A DATASHEET, and it says so: this is the load THIS DESIGN presents (two 18 pF capacitors give 9 pF in series and the pins and tracks add about 3), so the codec clock crystal that is bought must be specified at 12 pF. The generator's own comment has read 'to confirm on the EVM sheet' since D8 and it was never confirmed; the part choice is owner decision 37 and this declaration moves with it.

_via_sizing_why: MEASURED ON D12 AND OWED TO THE NEXT GENERATION, 17 September 2026 (rule PI-003). With the barrel currents dc_drop solved beside the board, one barrel of the four measured rails is over its own wall's rating: +5V_SA at (71.4, 74.2) carries 1.10 A of the solved mesh against 0.90 A for a 18 um wall at 10 K, a ratio of 1.22. It is a LAYER TRANSITION that wants a second barrel beside it, not a wider rail: two barrels there carry 0.55 A each. Board A's placement generator already reads `out/<stem>-via-currents.json` and reports a site whose MEASURED barrel is over its rating (gen_pcb_a3.py `_size`); board D's does not, so this note is the handover until it does. Nothing is patched onto D12: the board is held by decision 31, whose ruling is a schematic change at the two headset jacks, so the next D generation carries both. CORRECTION, 18 September 2026 18:10 CEST, from `barrel_sites.py`'s first run: board D has TWO barrels over their rating on +5V_SA and not one. `via_current` reports the WORST barrel per RAIL, so its line has been naming one all day; the rail crosses layers TWICE and each crossing is a single 0.40 mm barrel carrying the whole 1.10 A of the solved mesh, at board (-28.59, 25.81) and at (-31.15, 17.96). D15's locked copper answers the FIRST: its three parallel barrels sit between FB1 pad 2 and C5 pad 1, 1.13 and 3.51 mm from that transition. The SECOND has one pad of its own net within 6 mm (FB1 pad 2 at 5.26 mm) and U2 pad 1 at 2.48 mm and three U1 pads inside 5 mm, so it is a tighter corridor and it is not drawn. What D15 measures is therefore whether the second crossing survives at all: the router may not need it once the first is copper, and that is read on the finished board with `barrel_sites.py` rather than assumed either way.

safety_lines.hazard: the 30 W amplifier is keyed with the panel absent

_safety_lines_why: Board D carries the transmitter, so its one judged line is the inhibit into the key gate, and it holds it down itself. The other is a conductor that ends at a test point.
_d13_route_why: D13 (18 September 2026, /root/drf on the hub, today's tools): the PWR class via at 1.2/0.6 (PI-003), thermal vias in every exposed pad, the SENSE class, land-judged pin maps. Round 1: 0 hard, 2 unrouted of 133, 327 vias; the closers left the two; via_parallel found every solved barrel inside its rating (the class via answered +5V_SA's two barrels at the source); refused at the routed-board gate for the two opens; routeflow's via_costs remedy round runs as round 2. Its clamps still wait on decision 31, so its folder stays refused whatever the route does. Landed 02:10 UTC: round 2 worse, round 1 restored and finished again, hard 0, unrouted 2 (/PCM_VDD at R28, /X_SA_PD at R77), check_pcb_d PASS, netlist_board PASS 994, dc_drop and dc_density PASS 4 of 4, place_audit PASS; not adopted, D12 stays. CORRECTION 18 September 2026 10:50 CEST: D13 was NOT routed with the 1.2/0.6 power via. gen_pcb_d3.py set it on the board through the API and then wrote a second, hand-typed class table into the project file (PWR 0.8/0.4, no SENSE), and the project file is what the DSN export and every gate read: D13's DSN carried Via[0-3]_800:400_um for PWR and its board holds one 0.8/0.4 via on /+5V_SA. The generators build the project table from the one CLASSES table now (test_netclass_one_source), so the next D phase is the first that carries the 1.2/0.6 via and the SENSE class. via_parallel on the committed D12 (dry, reach 6 mm) answers one of the two +5V_SA barrels and finds no linkable site for the other at (68.8, 82.0): 198 of 208 candidates are within clearance of another net's track and the ten that are free have no clean link on F.Cu or B.Cu, so D's PI-003 stays the generator's.
_d14_route_why: D14 (18 September 2026 09:00 UTC, /root/drf14, $SP/d14.sh): D13's configuration regenerated now that gen_pcb_d3.py writes one class table into the project file: the first D route whose DSN carries the PWR via 1.2/0.6 (PI-003) and the SENSE class at 0.7/0.3. D13 (0 hard, 2 open) was routed on the old project table and measured nothing about the wider via. Judged against D12's 0/0 with PI-003 FAIL: if D14 lands 0/0 with via_current PASS it is board D's next phase; if it lands open, the trade the 1.2/0.6 via costs is measured for the first time. Its DSN (09:07 UTC) carries Via[0-3]_1200:600_um for PWR and Via[0-3]_700:300_um for SENSE with SENSE as a class of its own, which no D DSN before it did. RESULT, round 1 (09:54 UTC): 0 hard, NINE open of 133 nets, 321 vias; the closers took none of them (the stub router closed 0 of 9) and the finish was refused. The ladder on one board with one variable each: D12 routed 0/0 with a 0.8/0.4 power via in its DSN, D13 2 open with the same via (its project file carried the old table), D14 NINE open with the 1.2/0.6 via and the SENSE class the generator has been declaring since 18 September. **So the wider power via costs board D nine connections**, which is the number decision 9's 1.2 mm class never had for the VIA (the 1.2 mm TRACK's cost was measured on 13 September as six connections and nine hard). Round 2 runs with via_costs 100. The alternative to a class-wide via, and the one board A already uses for its rails, is to leave the class via at 0.8/0.4 and lay the two over-rated transitions as LOCKED 1.2/0.6 vias in the placement generator, where the geometry is known and the router simply routes to them; that is D15's shape if round 2 does not close the nine. ROUND 2 (11:28 UTC) came back TEN open, worse than round one's nine, so the supervisor kept round one's board and skipped its finish. DECIDED THE SAME HOUR: the PWR class via goes back to 0.8/0.4 in the generator. PI-003 is advisory, the two barrels it names carry 1.10 A against 0.90, and nine connections of 133 is not a price an advisory rule can ask; the answer it wants is locked copper at the two transitions, board D's own +5V_D8 pattern, drawn where the geometry is known. D15 is D12's routability with that copper and via_parallel in the finish.
_d15_route_why: D15 LANDED AND IT ANSWERS PI-003 (18 September 2026, three rounds, `/root/drf15`, frozen as `/root/drf15k`, sha c40bab6c78a0d091). D15 is D12's routability plus the generator's locked copper at the two `+5V_SA` layer transitions (two 0.5 mm spines and a three-point stitch placed from the current by `power_copper`, not hand-counted). **`via_current` on the frozen board reads 0 rails and 0 barrels over their rating of 4 measured rails**, where D12's own reading is one rail over at two barrels: the rule is answered on this board by copper the generator laid. ANA-001 PASS of 6, `check_pcb_d` ALL PASS, hard 0 of the fifteen types. **It costs ONE connection**: round 1 is 0 hard and 1 unrouted of 133 nets, rounds 2 and 3 came back 4 and worse and routeflow restored round 1. The open is `/PCM_VDD`, 10.72 mm between R28 pad 2 at (110.68, 105.80) and a 2.75 mm track of its own net at (120.58, 109.90), and it is a connection the router never made rather than a closure it nearly made: the continuation pass (80 passes) reads 1 open before and after, and the stub router prints `/PCM_VDD pad -> track FAILED`. That is why board D now declares the direct closer (see `finish._direct_close_why`), which board D had never needed because D12 was 0/0. Adoption waits on a board at 0 open: a phase that answers an ADVISORY-turned-blocker rule by costing a connection is not an improvement, and D12 stays declared until D15 (or D16) closes it.

prelay_groups.why: D19: every connection board D's closers have ever reported FAILED pad to pad, in one group. D17 left /LED_REC_K and /PCM_VCCR; D18 pre-laid exactly those, closed 5 of 5, and the router then left /HS2_BIAS_R, /HUB_DM1 and /HUB_DP1 instead; /PCM_VDD is D15's. The union is six nets and the arm asks one question: is board D's last handful of opens a set the router shuffles, or is there a sixth net waiting behind them?

_prelay_groups_why: D16 PRE-LAYS `/PCM_VDD` BECAUSE NOTHING CAN CLOSE IT AFTERWARDS (18 September 2026). D15 lands 0 hard and one open, a 10.72 mm gap between R28 pad 2 and a track of its own net, and on the FINISHED board every instrument refuses it: the continuation pass of the router reads 1 open before and after over 80 passes, the stub router prints FAILED, and `direct_close`, given the 12.0 mm reach this board now declares, TRIED the closure and had every shape refused by the DRC for a `solder_mask_bridge` against R34's two pads, which sit in the corridor on B.Cu. The board is full there by the time anyone asks. **On the PLACED board that corridor is empty**, which is the C10 lesson of 14 September word for word (a 249 mm net four routes in a row would not take, laid before the router on a board whose strips were still empty), so the net is pre-laid with the same stub router restricted to it, on the two layers this board routes on, and the stage is guarded: the board is kept only if the hard count does not rise. Board E's E15 and E16 are the caution, not a counter-example: there the pre-lay laid nothing because the block's lands are walled, and it cost nothing to try. If this lays the net, D16 is D12's routability with PI-003 answered and nothing open.
_rail_barrels_why: BOARD D HAS ONE SHORT CROSSING AT GENERATION AND IT IS FREE TO ANSWER (19 September 2026, `rail_barrels.py` dry run on BOTH live D trees, read-only): of 6 crossings over D's declared rails, five carry the barrels their current needs and ONE does not, `+5V_SA` at FB1 pad 2 (71.79, 77.67) with one 0.40 mm barrel for 1.10 A where two are needed, and the site test finds room for the second. D17 and D18 read the SAME one, which is what you would expect: nothing between them touched a barrel count. **This does not contradict D15's PI-003 answer.** `via_current` reads the SOLVED mesh after a route, where the router's own vias give the current more paths than the generator drew; `rail_crossings` reads the declared current at the source or load pad BEFORE anything is routed, which is the harder question and the one a generator can still answer. `via_parallel` has been paying for this crossing after every D route since D15; from D19 the chain lays it at generation instead, which is one locked barrel and no round.
_d19_prediction: D19'S PREDICTION, WRITTEN BEFORE IT RUNS (19 September 2026). Board D has never had more than four connections open at the router and the same small set keeps changing hands: D17 two, D18 four (three after the continuation), and the two arms' opens are DISJOINT. If those six connections are a set the router shuffles because they are the last to be served, pre-laying all six should land at 0 or 1 open and board D is finished. **If instead a SEVENTH net opens, the shuffling is not the cause**: the board is congested at the hub's fan and the answer is a placement change at U4 pad 11 and R13 pad 1, which is 2.82 mm with no lane and has been board D's open item since 11 September, when D10 needed it closed by hand. Either result settles it, which is why the arm is worth its two hours. THE CAVEAT: the pre-lay moves congestion rather than removing it, so a seventh net opening is the EXPECTED failure mode, not a surprise, and it must not be read as the pre-lay being broken.
_d19_router_result: D19'S ROUTER: HARD 0 AND TWO OPEN OF 133, WITH ALL SIX EVER-FAILED CONNECTIONS PRE-LAID AND CLOSED (19 September 2026, 200 passes in 2 h 29, 329 vias). **The prediction written before it ran has its answer and it is the second branch.** It said: if board D's last handful of opens is a set the router shuffles because they are served last, pre-laying all six lands at 0 or 1 and board D is finished; if instead a SEVENTH net opens, the shuffling is not the cause and the congestion is structural. The pre-lay closed 8 of 8 pairs across `/PCM_VDD`, `/LED_REC_K`, `/PCM_VCCR`, `/HS2_BIAS_R`, `/HUB_DM1` and `/HUB_DP1`, so **the two the router left are not among them**: two OTHER nets opened. **So board D's opens are not a serving-order effect.** Pre-laying six connections bought back the two D18 had lost and handed the same shortfall to two more, which is the same mechanism the D17/D18 pair showed at a smaller scale and board E showed at a larger one: a pre-lay closes what it targets and hands the congestion to its neighbours. Board D has a fixed amount of copper it cannot place, about two connections' worth, and it moves around the board depending on what is pinned. **The answer is the placement**, and the record has named the site since 11 September: the hub's own fan at U4 pad 11 and R13 pad 1, 2.82 mm apart with no lane, which D10 needed closed by hand. Read the closers before concluding: D17 and D18's stub routers both took none, and if D19's take these two the board closes at 0 and the whole argument changes.
_d19_result_why:
BOARD D LANDS AT TWO OPEN WHATEVER IS PINNED, AND THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT EVERY TIME (19 September 2026, D19's closers took neither of its two). Three arms, all 200 passes, same design, one variable:
  D17  one net pre-laid   router 2, closers 0, **2 open**: `/LED_REC_K`, `/PCM_VCCR`
  D18  three pre-laid     router 4, continuation 1, **3 open**: `/HS2_BIAS_R`, `/HUB_DM1`, `/HUB_DP1`
  D19  SIX pre-laid       router 2, closers 0, **2 open**: `/+5V_D8`, `/PCM_XTI`
**The three sets of opens are pairwise DISJOINT.** D19 pre-laid every connection board D's closers have ever reported FAILED pad to pad, closed 8 of 8 pairs, and the router answered by leaving a POWER RAIL and a CRYSTAL INPUT instead, neither of which had ever been open before. So the prediction written before the arm ran is answered on its second branch: **this is not a serving-order effect and no amount of pinning reaches it.** Board D has a fixed deficit of about two connections, and pinning decides only WHERE it lands. **D17 STAYS BOARD D'S ANSWER**: it reaches the same two open with ONE net pre-laid instead of six, so it is the simpler board and the pre-laid copper of D19 buys nothing. **The remaining work is the placement**, and the site is the one the record has named since 11 September, the hub's own fan at U4 pad 11 and R13 pad 1, 2.82 mm with no lane, which D10 closed by hand. Board D is two connections from a finished route and those two connections are a floor-plan item, which is the same sentence board B's much larger number resolves to.
_d_last_two_is_capacity_why: BOARD D'S LAST TWO CONNECTIONS ARE A CAPACITY QUESTION, WHICH NAMES THE DECISION THAT GOVERNS THEM (19 September 2026, after D19). It is tempting to read the remaining pair as one bad neighbourhood and go and move two resistors, and D19 is the measurement that says otherwise: the deficit is not AT a site, it MOVES. `/HUB_DM1` was the named site from 11 September and D19 pinned it, whereupon a power rail and a crystal input opened instead. Three arms, three disjoint pairs, always two. **So the board is about two connections short of the copper it needs, wherever you put them.** The levers for capacity are three and only three: a placement that frees corridors (board D's regions are already packed and `region_room` is the instrument), **a layer count**, or accepting two open.
